title: Improving a presentation: an algebra with retraction and free differentials on the smooth locus
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation. There are an $A$-algebra $C$ of finite type over $A$ (generated as an $A$-algebra by finitely many elements) and a homomorphism of $A$-algebras $\rho:C\to A$ (a retraction of $A\to C$) such that for every $a\in A$ for which $A_a$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], the localization $C_a$ (at the powers of the image of $a$) is a smooth $R$-algebra and $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is a free $C_a$-module. (For a presentation $A=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I$ one can take $C=\operatorname{Sym}^*_A(I/I^2)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] with $\rho$ the projection to degree $0$.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CE (lemma-improve-presentation, line 342) and its proof (C = Sym_A(I/I^2)): clause (2) gives Omega_{C_a/R} free when A_a is smooth; clause (1) gives C_a smooth over A_a when R -> A_a is a local complete intersection (More on Algebra, Definition 07D0), which holds for smooth A_a (Algebra, Lemma 00TA: smooth implies syntomic), so C_a is smooth over R by composition. The node states this combination, which is how the proof of Lemma 07FJ uses 07CE ('C_{x_i} is smooth over k[x_1,...,x_d] with finite free module of differentials').

proof.text: (Construction.) Choose a presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] $A=P/I$ with $P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and $I=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$. Put $M=I/I^2$, an $A$-module generated by the classes $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_m$, and $C=\operatorname{Sym}_A(M)$ with $\iota_M:M\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. By the universal property applied to the zero map $M\to A$ there is a unique $A$-algebra homomorphism $\rho:C\to A$ with $\rho\circ\iota_M=0$ (the projection to the degree-$0$ part); being a homomorphism of $A$-algebras, $\rho$ composed with the structure map $A\to C$ is $\mathrm{id}_A$, so $\rho$ is a retraction. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-presentation](a), $C$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by $\iota_M(\bar f_1),\dots,\iota_M(\bar f_m)$, so $C$ is of finite type over $A$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE, lines 357-366 (choice of presentation, C = Sym_A(I/I^2), retraction = projection to degree 0)

proof.text: (Localizing.) Fix $a\in A$ with $A_a$ smooth over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $h\in P$ mapping to $a$. Since $C_a$ (localization at the image of $a$) is $A_a\otimes_AC$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor], [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] (with $S=A_a$) gives an isomorphism of $A_a$-algebras $C_a\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{A_a}(M_a)$, where $M_a=A_a\otimes_AM=(I/I^2)_a$ is generated by the images of $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_m$; it is compatible with the retractions ($\rho_a:C_a\to A_a$ is the degree-$0$ projection).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE, lines 380-392 (localized rings A_a and C_a)

proof.text: ($(I/I^2)_a$ is finite projective and $(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\cong A_a^{\oplus n}$.) Let $\alpha:P\to A$ be the presentation of step 1 and $\beta:P[x_0]\to A_a$ the presentation extending it with $x_0\mapsto1/a$; by [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent] $\beta$ is surjective with kernel $I'=(hx_0-1,I)$. The ring map $R\to P[x_0]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], so [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-quotient-smooth] (with $A\to B\to C$ there being $R\to P[x_0]\to A_a$, $\mathfrak a=I'$) gives an exact sequence $0\to H_1(L_{A_a/R})\to I'/I'^2\to A_a\otimes_{P[x_0]}\Omega_{P[x_0]/R}\to\Omega_{A_a/R}\to0$, whose middle map is the map of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$. As $A_a$ is smooth over $R$, $H_1(L_{A_a/R})=0$ and $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ is finite projective [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; so the map of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ is injective with cokernel $\Omega_{A_a/R}$. By the 'in particular' of [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent] the map $(I/I^2)_a\to\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PA_a$ of $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_AA_a$, $\bar f\mapsto\mathrm df\otimes1$, is injective with cokernel $\cong\Omega_{A_a/R}$, and $\Omega_{P/R}\otimes_PA_a=\bigoplus_{i=1}^nA_a\,\mathrm dx_i$ is free [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis]. A surjection onto the projective module $\Omega_{A_a/R}$ splits, so $(I/I^2)_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\cong A_a^{\oplus n}$; in particular $M_a=(I/I^2)_a$ is a direct summand of $A_a^{\oplus n}$, i.e. finite projective.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE, lines 381-392 (presentation I' = (hx_0 - 1, I), I'/(I')^2 = A_a + (I/I^2)_a) and lines 438-439 ('(I/I^2)_a + Omega_{A_a/R} is free (from the definition of smooth ring maps)'); in Stacks' clause (1) the finite projectivity of (I/I^2)_a comes from the lci hypothesis (lines 404-407), which in the smooth case is replaced by this step

proof.text: ($C_a$ is smooth over $R$.) By step 3, $M_a$ is a finite projective $A_a$-module, so $A_a\to\operatorname{Sym}_{A_a}(M_a)\cong C_a$ (step 2) is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-finite-projective-smooth]. As $R\to A_a$ is smooth, the composite $R\to A_a\to C_a$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition](2).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CE, clause (1) ('the ring C_a is smooth over A_a', lines 344-349), proved here from step 3 and More on Algebra Lemma Tag 07M6 (Sym of a finite projective module is smooth); smooth over R by composition, as the node's source says

proof.text: ($\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is free.) The Jacobi--Zariski sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence] for $R\to A_a\to C_a$ ends with the exact sequence $H_1(L_{C_a/A_a})\to C_a\otimes_{A_a}\Omega_{A_a/R}\to\Omega_{C_a/R}\to\Omega_{C_a/A_a}\to0$, and $H_1(L_{C_a/A_a})=0$ because $A_a\to C_a$ is smooth (step 4, [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]); so $0\to C_a\otimes_{A_a}\Omega_{A_a/R}\to\Omega_{C_a/R}\to\Omega_{C_a/A_a}\to0$ is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra] to $A_a$, the surjection $A_a^{\oplus m}\to M_a$, $e_j\mapsto\bar f_j$, and its kernel: $\Omega_{C_a/A_a}\cong M_a\otimes_{A_a}C_a$, which is a finite projective $C_a$-module (base change of the finite projective $M_a$, step 3). Hence the sequence splits and $\Omega_{C_a/R}\cong C_a\otimes_{A_a}(\Omega_{A_a/R}\oplus M_a)\cong C_a\otimes_{A_a}A_a^{\oplus n}=C_a^{\oplus n}$ by step 3; so $\Omega_{C_a/R}$ is a free $C_a$-module. (This is the module $I/I^2\otimes_AC_a\oplus\Omega_{A_a/R}\otimes_{A_a}C_a$ found in Stacks.) Together with step 4 and step 1 this proves the lemma.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CE, lines 367-379 (Algebra 00S2 for R -> A -> C and More on Algebra 07EV) and lines 419-440 (Omega_{C_a/R} = I/I^2 (x)_A C_a + Omega_{A_a/R} (x)_{A_a} C_a, free since (I/I^2)_a + Omega_{A_a/R} is free); the injectivity of C_a (x) Omega_{A_a/R} -> Omega_{C_a/R}, which Stacks takes from the left exactness of clause (1) (More on Algebra lemma-transitive-lci-at-end), is here H_1(L_{C_a/A_a}) = 0 for the smooth A_a -> C_a

split_report.summary: Statement kept (two clarifying additions: 'finite type' spelled out, Sym cited); stmt_deps now name finite presentation, smooth, Kähler differentials, Sym. Proof in five steps following Stacks 07CE: construction C = Sym_A(I/I^2) with degree-0 retraction and finite type; C_a = Sym_{A_a}((I/I^2)_a); finite projectivity of (I/I^2)_a and (I/I^2)_a + Omega_{A_a/R} = A_a^n from the presentation of A_a with hx_0 - 1 (Algebra 08JZ, new node) and the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for a quotient of a polynomial ring (existing node, 00S2/07BP) together with smoothness of A_a ('from the definition of smooth ring maps', Stacks line 439); C_a smooth over A_a by Sym of finite projective (07M6 node) and over R by composition; Omega_{C_a/R} free from 00S2 (existing node) for R -> A_a -> C_a and 07EV (new node). Since the node only claims the smooth case, the local-complete-intersection machinery of Stacks' clause (1) (07D0, quasi-regular-ideal-finite-projective, transitive-lci-at-end, 00TA) is not needed: what Stacks gets from it (finite projectivity of (I/I^2)_a, injectivity of C_a (x) Omega_{A_a/R} -> Omega_{C_a/R}) comes from smoothness of A_a and of C_a over A_a. New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent (08JZ; Mathlib has clause (1) only), lem-weil-pbc-cotangent-complex-symmetric-algebra (07EV; not in Mathlib).

reviewed.note: 5 steps follow Stacks 07CE restricted to the smooth case (the lci clause is not part of the statement): C = Sym_A(I/I^2) with retraction; C_a = Sym_{A_a}((I/I^2)_a); (I/I^2)_a finite projective with (I/I^2)_a + Omega_{A_a/R} = A_a^n via the new 08JZ node and the Jacobi-Zariski quotient node; C_a smooth over A_a (Sym of finite projective) and over R; Omega_{C_a/R} free via the Jacobi-Zariski sequence and the new 07EV node. Statement citations added (finitely presented, Sym). Tags 07CE, 08JZ, 07EV, 00S2 verified.

lean.statement: theorem exists_finiteType_retract_smooth_free_differentials (R : Type u) (A : Type v) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A] [FinitePresentation R A] : ∃ (C : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing C) (_ : Algebra A C), letI : Algebra R C := ((algebraMap A C).comp (algebraMap R A)).toAlgebra FiniteType A C ∧ ∃ ρ : C →ₐ[A] A, (∀ x : A, ρ (algebraMap A C x) = x) ∧ ∀ a : A, Smooth R (Localization.Away a) → Smooth R (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a)) ∧ Module.Free (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a)) (KaehlerDifferential R (Localization.Away (algebraMap A C a)))
lean.note: The first declaration states existence; the second renders the parenthetical construction for every finite polynomial presentation, with C = Sym_A(I/I²) and ρ = SymmetricAlgebra.lift 0.

reviewed_lean.note: R,A CommRing + Algebra + FinitePresentation; ∃ C : Type (max u v) A-algebra, R-structure = composite (rfl-checked through Localization.Away); FiniteType A C; ρ : C →ₐ[A] A retraction; ∀ a, Smooth R A_a → Smooth R C_a ∧ Module.Free C_a Ω[C_a/R]; parenthetical: Presentation R A (Fin n vars) (Fin m rels), C = SymmetricAlgebra A P.toExtension.Cotangent (I/I²), ρ = lift 0
